goal.title: W state on 4 qubits
goal.blurb: One excitation shared equally by four qubits: the state that keeps its entanglement when a qubit is lost, used in quantum networks.

proposals.why: Star fan-out from qubit 0 can distribute a single excitation equally to all qubits as in standard W-state constructions.
Linear chain sequentially splits excitation amplitude to build the equal one-hot superposition across four qubits.
Chain plus closing edge adds symmetric entanglement to balance amplitudes beyond a minimal tree.
Pairwise entangling blocks with full connectivity provide enough expressivity to guarantee W-state preparation if minimal circuits fail.
This is the 4-gate prefix of the proven 6-gate solution and may already span the entanglement needed for the symmetric W state.
This drops only the final gate of the proven 6-gate solution to test whether that last entangler was redundant.
This K4-minus-one simple graph gives maximally symmetric pairwise connectivity suited to the permutation-symmetric W state.
This uses the same symmetric 5-pair set in chain-first order to distribute the single excitation sequentially around all qubits.
Keeps the proven cross-pairing and final reuse while testing if the first [0,1] is redundant.
Preserves the double [0,1] balancing pair from the proven 5-CNOT circuit while dropping the [2,3] seed.
Retains both initial pairs and the repeated [0,1] while testing if [0,2] can be removed.
Retains both initial pairs and the repeated [0,1] while testing if [1,3] can be removed.
Middle-first chain spreads entanglement outward symmetrically which should distribute the single excitation to all four qubits.
Repairs the closest 4-CNOT near miss by interleaving the repeated 0-1 pair earlier to adjust interference before coupling to qubit 3.
Linear chain with a central repeat adds the missing degree of freedom to balance the W-state amplitudes across the ends.
Symmetric star fan-out from qubit 0 with one extra entangler should create equal single-excitation superposition.
Reorders the star-like near miss to entangle qubits 1 and 2 first with a repeated bridge before fanning out to qubit 3.
Swaps the middle cross-links of the closest 4-CNOT near miss to balance entanglement creation across both qubit pairs.
Clusters the repeated chain bridge together to build the delocalized excitation locally before spreading it to the end qubit.
Forms the alternate 4-cycle covering all qubits exactly once to symmetrically delocalize the single excitation for the W state.
A linear spanning path links all four qubits with the minimal three entanglers and matches sequential single-excitation spreading for the W state.
A star centered on qubit 0 distributes entanglement symmetrically to the three leaves, matching the permutation symmetry of the W state.
A four-qubit ring adds one cyclic entangler beyond a tree to boost expressibility while keeping pairwise connectivity.
Doubling each chain edge provides two CNOTs per particle-conserving split, realizing the known deterministic three-split construction of W4.
W4 has Schmidt rank 2 across every cut so a star centered on qubit 0 gives three rank-2 links enough bond dimension to build it with three CNOTs.
The symmetric W4 state has bipartite rank 2 everywhere so a star centered on qubit 1 can concentrate and distribute the single excitation with one CNOT per leaf.
W4 admits an exact matrix-product form with bond dimension 2 so a linear chain propagating the excitation needs only one CNOT per bond.
Sequential Schmidt decomposition from qubit 0 outward has rank 2 at each step so the ordered path builds the single-excitation superposition with three single-CNOT isometries.
Star centered on qubit 0 fans out one excitation to all 4 qubits with the minimal 3 links needed for symmetric W entanglement.
Linear chain sequentially splits the single excitation to accumulate four equal one-hot terms with only 3 CNOTs.
Middle-out tree starts entanglement in the center then spreads outward to balance the four W amplitudes symmetrically.
Chain plus closing link adds one extra entangler to guarantee exact fitting of the W4 amplitudes if 3 CNOTs are marginal.
Linear chain incrementally adds one new qubit per CNOT with Schmidt rank two across each cut which matches the W state entanglement.
Alternate chain spans all four qubits so sequential single-excitation splitting can distribute equal weight to each computational basis term.
Star centered on qubit zero fans out from a single source so central rotations plus three CNOTs can create the symmetric single-excitation superposition.
Star centered on qubit one connects every qubit in a spanning tree so each CNOT introduces a new qubit while preserving rank-two bipartitions needed for W4.
Middle-out chain seeds entanglement in the center then expands symmetrically to distribute a single excitation over all four qubits with a minimal spanning tree.
Paired entanglers followed by cross-links capture the 2-versus-2 rank-2 structure of the W state with one extra degree for exact amplitudes.
Hub-centered fan-out from qubit 0 plus one leaf-leaf entangler breaks star symmetry just enough to balance the four single-excitation terms.
Six-CNOT complete pairwise sequence guarantees enough expressivity to realize the symmetric single-excitation Dicke state exactly.

goal.title: Dicke state |D(4,2)⟩
goal.blurb: Every way of having exactly two of four qubits at 1, in equal superposition: a resource for quantum sensing beyond the standard limit.

proposals.why: Star fan-out from qubit 0 meets the two-crossing per 2-2 cut needed for Schmidt rank 3 with the minimum 3 CNOTs.
Four-cycle ring preserves cyclic symmetry natural for the permutation-symmetric Dicke state while adding one entangler beyond the lower bound.
Five entanglers combine a Schmidt-satisfying star with leaf-leaf interactions to generate the weight-2 symmetrization.
Six CNOTs covering every qubit pair once give full connectivity and ample parameters known to suffice for D4^2-type circuits.
Drops only the last pair from the proven 6-CNOT complete graph while keeping disjoint initial entanglers and full cross connectivity.
Keeps the proven disjoint start and cross middle but closes with the final proven pair to build symmetric weight-2 interference with 5 CNOTs.
Uses a different ordering of K4-minus-one that interleaves cross pairs early to generate rank-3 Schmidt components on every 2-2 split.
Minimal balanced 4-CNOT layout with exactly two crossing CNOTs on each 2-2 bipartition starting from disjoint pairs.
Uses two disjoint initial pairs then three crosses missing only (0,2), the one 5-distinct set not yet tried.
Reorders the 5-distinct set missing (2,3) to interleave the crosses differently for better optimizer reach.
Repeats the central (0,2) cross to add extra Schmidt rank across the 01|23 partition with only 5 CNOTs.
Forms a 4-qubit ring then reuses (0,1) to build symmetric Dicke entanglement with repeated-pair expressivity.
Mimics the proven 5-CNOT chain with a closing repeat of the first pair to symmetrize amplitudes into the equal weight-2 superposition.
Uses two complementary pair groups to give two crossing CNOTs for every 2-2 bipartition that needs Schmidt rank 3.
Builds full symmetric entanglement on qubits 0-1-2 as a triangle then spreads it to qubit 3 for Dicke symmetrization.
Tests the minimal linear spanning-tree alternative to the failed star, as any 3-CNOT solution must be connected.
Sandwiching the outer arms around a doubled central 1-2 link keeps two crossings on every 2-vs-2 cut needed for the rank-3 Dicke state.
Centering on qubit 0 with a doubled 0-1 arm sandwiched around the star distributes the symmetric weight-2 entanglement while meeting all bipartition ranks.
Building a star from 0 then closing the 0-1-2 triangle with 1-2 forms a diamond that preserves at least two crossings on each balanced cut.
Doubling the middle 1-2 link consecutively at the end of the path tests a different ordering of the viable path-double-middle graph.
A star centered on qubit 0 is the only 3-edge connected graph giving two crossing CNOTs on every 2-versus-2 bipartition as required by the rank-3 Schmidt spectrum of the weight-2 Dicke state.
A four-qubit ring adds a fourth entangling gate to the minimal star while preserving two crossings on every bipartition to provide extra freedom for balancing the six weight-2 amplitudes.
Adding a diagonal to the ring creates denser all-to-all entanglement to tune the symmetric superposition with five CNOTs while keeping every qubit connected.
Using all six distinct pairs once gives a fully connected all-to-all circuit with ample parameters to realize the symmetric Dicke-4-2 state exactly if fewer CNOTs prove insufficient.
Star centered on qubit 0 links every qubit and puts two CNOTs across each 2-versus-2 cut to allow Schmidt rank three for the Dicke state.
Four-CNOT ring alternates halves so every 2-versus-2 bipartition sees at least two crossing CNOTs while keeping the circuit symmetric under qubit permutation.
Five-CNOT ring plus a diagonal adds extra entanglement across the middle cut to realize the three Schmidt coefficients with margin for the optimizer.
Six-CNOT all-to-all sequence touches every qubit pair to guarantee enough expressivity to build the six weight-two amplitudes exactly.
Star with center 0 connects all 4 qubits with 3 CNOTs and gives exactly 2 crossings of every 2-2 bipartition required for the Schmidt rank-3 of the weight-2 Dicke state.
4-qubit ring adds a cycle to the spanning tree to symmetrize entanglement across all 2-2 cuts while keeping CNOT count minimal.
Near-complete graph gives at least 3 CNOTs across every 2-2 bipartition, allowing tunable rank-3 Schmidt coefficients for the symmetric weight distribution.
Complete K4 pairwise entangling mirrors the permutation symmetry of all 6 weight-2 basis states and guarantees full rank across all bipartitions.
Uses each unordered pair once to respect full permutation symmetry of the Dicke D4^2 state and give every 2-2 bipartition crossing entanglers for Schmidt rank 3.
Double linear staircase mirrors the standard SCS Dicke preparation that builds weight-2 excitations sequentially along the chain.
Repeated star centered on qubit 0 first distributes one excitation as in W-state preparation then adds the second excitation symmetrically.
Ring plus cross-links creates balanced entanglement across all 1-3 and 2-2 cuts needed for uniform weight-2 superposition.
Two disjoint CNOTs can form (|01>+|10>) pairs giving the four middle terms while two cross CNOTs mix in |0011> and |1100>.
Star centered on qubit 0 is the minimal tree meeting Schmidt rank 3 on all 2-2 cuts and rank 2 on all 1-3 cuts.
Two Bell-pair CNOTs plus three inter-pair CNOTs provide enough mixing to balance all six weight-2 amplitudes equally.
Covering all six pairs gives a fully connected entangler that can symmetrize two Bell pairs into the Dicke D4_2 state.

goal.title: W state on 5 qubits in a line
goal.blurb: One excitation shared by five qubits, each wired only to its neighbours: no textbook circuit fits, so the layout has to be found.

proposals.why: Sequential cascade from the top distributes the single excitation with one CNOT per new qubit matching the spanning-tree lower bound
Mirror sweep from the bottom provides the same n-minus-1 entangling steps in opposite order for the symmetric W state
Center-out branching creates both sides of the chain from the middle to fit the symmetric Schmidt structure
Doubled cascade implements each controlled splitting exactly to guarantee reachability if minimal layouts fail
Bottom-up cascade needs only one CNOT for the initial product-state split and two CNOTs per later excitation-preserving split, giving 7 CNOTs.
Top-down cascade mirrors the proven 8-CNOT circuit but saves one CNOT on the first edge where bipartite entanglement needs only one CNOT.
Tests whether the two least-entangled end cuts can use single CNOTs while keeping doubled CNOTs on the more entangled middle cuts.
Flipped-control version of the 6-CNOT cascade explores the opposite CNOT direction for spreading the excitation from the top end.
Doubling the two outer links instead of the inner links balances the distribution of the single excitation to the ends of the line.
Shifting the doubled pairs to edges 0-1 and 2-3 tests the asymmetric 2-1-2-1 distribution not yet tried for 6 CNOTs.
A triple on the central-adjacent edge gives a universal two-qubit block that can create the initial tripartite W-type split.
Keeping 1-2-2-1 counts but spreading center-out from qubit 2 repairs the failed linear cascade ordering with a branching order.
Keeps the promising 1-2-2-1 edge counts but builds the spanning tree first then reinforces the middle splits.
Tests asymmetric 1-2-1-2 distribution with sequential order to weight the q4 end more heavily.
Tests opposite asymmetric 2-2-1-1 distribution concentrating two-CNOT splits near the q0 end.
Starts from central qubit 2 for symmetric W-state fan-out then reapplies central splits to balance amplitudes.
Trims one CNOT on edge 1-2 from the proven 7-CNOT top-down chain while preserving order and all-cut entanglement.
Trims one CNOT on edge 1-2 from the proven 7-CNOT bottom-up chain while preserving order and all-cut entanglement.
Repairs the closest 0.088 sweep miss by returning symmetrically inward to better balance the outer W amplitudes.
Repairs the central-hub 0.088 miss by preparing outer leaves first then reusing the middle hub twice to spread one excitation.
A linear cascade from qubit 0 uses one CNOT for the initial two-qubit W pair and two CNOTs for each further particle-conserving split to spread the single excitation across all five qubits.
The mirror cascade from qubit 4 uses one CNOT for the initial pair and two CNOTs per subsequent controlled split to distribute the excitation over the whole chain.
Starting from the central link keeps depth low while providing one CNOT for the seed entanglement and two CNOTs per added branch to reach all five qubits symmetrically.
Doubling every chain link supplies two CNOTs per edge which suffices to realize every required controlled rotation for exact W-state preparation.
Cascades a single excitation from qubit 4 down the line using two CNOTs per edge to realize each particle-conserving split for the W5 state.
Cascades a single excitation from qubit 0 up the line using two CNOTs per edge to realize each particle-conserving split for the W5 state.
Starts from the middle qubit and fans out both ways with two CNOTs per edge to distribute one excitation uniformly with balanced depth.
Covers every line edge twice with alternating CNOT directions to provide full two-qubit entangling power for sequential W5 splitting steps.
Sequential cascade from qubit 4 distributes the single excitation across all four linear cuts with one entangling gate per cut, matching the Schmidt rank 2 required for the W state.
Reverse cascade propagates the excitation from qubit 0 outward covering each bipartition once, giving full rank-2 entanglement with minimal depth.
Starting from the central qubit balances the Schmidt coefficients on both sides and uses each chain edge exactly once to generate symmetric W entanglement.
Doubling each edge implements the standard deterministic W-state splitter sequence where each pair synthesizes an arbitrary excitation-preserving controlled rotation.
Linear sweep crosses each of the four chain bipartitions exactly once, giving the required Schmidt rank 2 everywhere with the minimal four entanglers.
Chain sweep plus two extra central CNOTs boosts the middle cut where W5 entanglement is largest while keeping count near minimal.
Doubling every chain edge allows each sequential excitation-splitting controlled rotation to be realized, implementing the standard deterministic W-state cascade.
Center-out doubled pairs form a balanced excitation-distribution tree from qubit 2 that realizes all beam-splitter angles with low depth.
Forward sequential MPS staircase from qubit 0 crosses each linear cut once giving Schmidt rank 2 matching all W-state bipartitions.
Reverse sequential build from qubit 4 crosses each cut once and realizes the recursive single-excitation peeling decomposition of W5.
Middle-seeded growth expands an entangled pair outward to both ends while keeping bond dimension 2 across every cut.
Doubled staircase provides a full excitation-preserving Givens rotation per edge guaranteeing exact sequential distribution of one excitation.
